description: 20 standardized enterprise queries across 4 categories. The `expected` blocks are not scored in Week 1; they are reference data for the Week 2 scorers.
default_system_prompt: You are a precise assistant for enterprise workflows. Follow the output format exactly and do not add commentary unless asked.

queries.title: Incident postmortem
queries.prompt:
Summarize the following incident report in exactly 3 bullet points covering impact, root cause, and follow-up actions.

Incident INC-4471 (2026-10-14): Between 09:12 and 10:47 SGT, roughly 18% of checkout requests in the APAC region failed with HTTP 503. The payments service exhausted its database connection pool after a config deploy reduced max_connections from 200 to 20; the change was meant for the staging environment only. On-call engineers rolled back the config at 10:31 and error rates returned to baseline by 10:47. Estimated lost revenue is SGD 42,000. Follow-ups: add environment validation to the config pipeline, alert when pool utilization exceeds 85%, and require a second approver for production config changes.

queries.title: Meeting transcript to decisions
queries.prompt:
Extract the decisions and action items (with owners and due dates) from this meeting transcript. Respond with two headed lists: 'Decisions' and 'Action items'.

Priya: We're agreed the Q1 launch moves from Jan 15 to Feb 3, mainly because the SOC 2 audit isn't closing until late January.
Marcus: Yes. I'll update the customer comms and send them by Friday, Nov 7.
Priya: Lena, can you re-plan the beta cohort? We still want 40 design partners.
Lena: Sure, I'll have the revised list by Nov 12.
Marcus: And we're dropping the on-prem SKU from the launch entirely; we'll revisit in Q2.
Priya: Agreed. I'll brief the board on Nov 10.

decisions: Launch moves from Jan 15 to Feb 3
On-prem SKU dropped from launch, revisit Q2

action_items.task: Revised beta cohort list (40 design partners)

queries.title: Policy change for employees
queries.prompt:
Rewrite this policy update as a plain-language summary for employees in no more than 60 words.

Effective 1 December 2026, the Travel & Expense Policy (TEP-v7) is amended as follows: (a) economy class is mandatory for all flights under 6 hours irrespective of grade; (b) premium economy is permitted for flights of 6 hours or more for grades M3 and above; (c) hotel nightly caps are revised to SGD 280 for Singapore and USD 250 for all other locations; (d) expense claims must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the trip end date, after which claims require VP approval.

queries.title: Customer feedback themes
queries.prompt:
Identify the top 3 themes in this customer feedback and give a one-sentence description of each, ordered by frequency.

1. "The SSO setup took us two weeks, documentation was outdated."
2. "Love the dashboards, but exports to Excel break with large datasets."
3. "Okta integration was painful; your guide references old screens."
4. "Pricing jumped 30% at renewal without much notice."
5. "CSV export times out above 100k rows."
6. "Support was quick, but the SAML docs are wrong."
7. "Renewal quote was a shock; we need more lead time on price changes."
8. "Export to Excel loses formatting and fails on big reports."

themes_in_order: Renewal price increases with little notice (2)

queries.title: Executive one-liner from quarterly memo
queries.prompt:
Write a single-sentence executive summary (max 35 words) of this memo.

Q3 FY26 results: revenue was USD 18.4M, up 22% year over year, driven by enterprise expansion (net revenue retention 124%). Gross margin fell 3 points to 71% due to higher inference compute costs from the new AI assistant feature. Operating cash flow turned positive for the first time at USD 1.1M. Headcount grew from 182 to 196. Management expects compute costs per user to fall 30% in Q4 after migrating to a cheaper model tier.

queries.title: Meeting slot constraints
queries.prompt: Three meetings (A, B, C) must be scheduled in the 9:00, 10:00 and 11:00 slots, one per slot. Meeting A cannot be at 9:00. Meeting C must be immediately after meeting B. What time is each meeting? Show your reasoning briefly, then give the final answer on the last line as 'A=HH:MM, B=HH:MM, C=HH:MM'.

queries.title: Annual licence cost
queries.prompt: A SaaS plan costs USD 40 per seat per month. Annual billing gets a 15% discount on the full year. A team of 12 seats chooses annual billing. What is the total annual cost? Show your working briefly, then give the final answer on the last line as a number only.

queries.title: SLA breach
queries.prompt: A service has a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA, measured over a 30-day month. In October it had a single outage lasting 50 minutes. Was the SLA breached, and by how many minutes over (or under) the allowed downtime? Show your working briefly, then give the final answer on the last line as 'BREACHED by X minutes' or 'MET with X minutes to spare'.

queries.title: Vendor syllogism
queries.prompt:
Facts: (1) All approved vendors have passed a security review. (2) Some vendors that passed a security review are based in the EU. (3) Vendor Q is approved.
Question 1: Can we conclude that Vendor Q passed a security review?
Question 2: Can we conclude that Vendor Q is based in the EU?
Answer each with Yes or No and a one-sentence justification. Give the final answer on the last line as 'Q1=Yes|No, Q2=Yes|No'.

queries.title: Invoice due date
queries.prompt: An invoice dated 28 March 2026 has payment terms of Net 45 (due 45 calendar days after the invoice date). What is the due date? Show your working briefly, then give the final answer on the last line in YYYY-MM-DD format.

queries.title: Business days between dates
queries.prompt: Write a Python 3.11 function `business_days_between(start: date, end: date, holidays: set[date]) -> int` that counts weekdays (Mon-Fri) from `start` inclusive to `end` exclusive, skipping any dates in `holidays`. Return 0 if end <= start. Use only the standard library. Return only the code in a single ```python block.

queries.title: Top customers per region (SQL)
queries.prompt: Given PostgreSQL tables customers(id, name, region) and orders(id, customer_id, amount numeric, created_at timestamptz), write a single SQL query that returns the top 3 customers by total order amount in each region over the last 90 days, with columns region, customer_name, total_amount, rank. Ties should share a rank. Return only the SQL in a single ```sql block.

queries.title: Deduplicate customer records
queries.prompt: Write a Python 3.11 function `dedupe_by_email(records: list[dict]) -> list[dict]` where each record has keys 'email' (str) and 'updated_at' (ISO 8601 str). Emails match case-insensitively and ignoring surrounding whitespace. Keep only the most recently updated record for each email, preserving the order in which each email first appears. Return only the code in a single ```python block.

queries.title: Async retry decorator
queries.prompt: Write a Python 3.11 decorator `retry_async(max_attempts: int = 3, base_delay: float = 0.5, exceptions: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = (Exception,))` for async functions. It retries on the given exceptions with exponential backoff (base_delay * 2**(attempt-1)) plus up to 10% random jitter, and re-raises the last exception after max_attempts. Preserve the wrapped function's metadata and add type hints. Return only the code in a single ```python block.

queries.title: PII masking
queries.prompt: Write a Python 3.11 function `mask_pii(text: str) -> str` that replaces email addresses with '[EMAIL]' and phone numbers (international format like +65 9123 4567 or +1 415-555-0100) with '[PHONE]'. Leave all other text unchanged. Use the `re` module. Return only the code in a single ```python block.
